stories.title: 'Fascinating' rare beetle found in Wales again after 60 years
summary: It was feared The Short-Necked Oil Beetle had become extinct in Wales after recent surveys

stories.title: Common pesticide linked to 2.5 times the risk of Parkinson’s disease
summary: A UCLA study found that long-term exposure to a common pesticide was linked to more than 2.5 times the risk of Parkinson's disease.
Scientists also uncovered how the chemical damages brain cells and identified a promising way to protect them.

stories.title: Aquarium shark that helped 'dispel myths' dies
summary: Staff at Plymouth's aquarium pay tribute to a sand tiger shark believed to be almost 30 years old.

stories.title: Scientists shrink Archimedes’ screw to the size of a single molecule
summary: Scientists have built a groundbreaking molecular motor that spins in either direction using electricity, inspired by a machine invented more than 2,000 years ago.
Even more remarkably, its rotation can boost electrical conductivity by up to 100 times, potentially transforming the future of molecular electronics.

stories.title: Scientists use sound waves to deliver a new attack on deadly brain cancer
summary: Scientists at the University of Virginia have developed a promising new strategy to fight glioblastoma, one of the deadliest and most difficult-to-treat forms of brain cancer.
Their experimental approach combines focused ultrasound, tiny nanoparticles, and genetic molecules called microRNAs to attack multiple cancer-driving genes simultaneously.

stories.title: Ancient ape fossil in Egypt could rewrite the story of human origins
summary: A 17- to 18-million-year-old ape fossil discovered in Egypt is challenging long-held beliefs about where the ancestors of humans and other modern apes first evolved.
Scientists now suspect that North Africa and the Middle East, rather than East Africa, may have been the cradle of modern ape evolution.

stories.title: Spill from vandalised home oil tank kills 13 birds
summary: A number of birds are also injured after the spill from the oil tank earlier this week.

stories.title: Rhino siblings celebrate first birthday with cake
summary: Markus and Mo weighed about 70kg (11st) at birth, and now weigh about 500kg (78st) each.

stories.title: Oil tank vandalism results in waterfowl park 'nightmare'
summary: The popular attraction in County Down has been forced to close while efforts continue to remove oil from the pond.

stories.title: 'Rok' solid recognition for Slovenian space scientist
summary: Two men from the Armagh Planetarium and Observatory have had asteroids named in their honour in recognition of their work.

stories.title: Rare damselfly spotted by restored chalk river
summary: The Herts and Middlesex Trust says it is "thrilled" the new wetlands are helping species thrive.

stories.title: Scientists say a forgotten particle may explain why the universe exists
summary: A mysterious particle overlooked for decades may hold the key to why matter survived the Big Bang, allowing stars, planets, and life to exist.
Scientists believe this forgotten neutrino reshaped the early universe and may have left detectable gravitational wave signals that could help unlock the cosmos’s deepest mysteries.

stories.title: Scientists discover the hidden “muscles” trees use to straighten themselves
summary: Scientists have discovered that trees can sense their own shape and straighten their trunks using specialized wood that acts like opposing muscles.
This remarkable ability helps trees maintain their posture and could lead to stronger forests, better timber, and more resilient crops.
